narrative:
On October 16, 2026, the Karnataka High Court scheduled 3,046 cases across 68 judge rosters and heard 1,221 matters, achieving an overall hearing rate of 40.1%. This performance reflects a slight increase in hearing efficiency compared to October 15 (38.8% of 3,217 cases heard) and October 14 (39.5% of 2,946 cases heard), though it remains below the 42.6% rate recorded on October 9.

Judicial output varied across courtrooms. Justice Sachin Shankar Magadum led in total hearings by addressing 94 out of 146 scheduled cases (64.4%). High conversion rates were also achieved by Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar, who heard 52 of 65 listed matters (80.0%), and Justice V. Srishananda, who heard 57 of 81 cases (70.4%). In contrast, several heavy rosters experienced lower throughput; Justice B.M. Shyam Prasad heard 11 of 123 scheduled cases (8.9%) on his primary list, while Justice S.R. Krishna Kumar heard 2 of 102 cases (2.0%) on his main roster.

Stage-wise analysis reveals that Preliminary Hearings achieved the highest conversion among major procedural stages at 52.0% (184 of 354 heard), followed by Admission at 43.1% (310 of 719 heard) and Orders at 41.8% (437 of 1,045 heard). Final Hearings recorded a 30.3% conversion rate (108 of 357 heard), marking an improvement over October 15 (25.2%) and October 14 (20.2%). Across case categories, Writ Petitions (WP) formed the bulk of the docket with 1,295 cases scheduled and a 34.3% hearing rate. Criminal Petitions (CRL.P) and Miscellaneous First Appeals (MFA) saw higher clearance at 42.6% (241 of 566) and 47.5% (184 of 387), respectively, while Criminal Appeals (CRL.A) reached a 66.7% clearance rate.
